short: Italy has a national AI law, Law No. 132 of 23 September 2025, in force since 10 October 2025, alongside the EU AI Act; its first implementing decree, Legislative Decree No. 179 of 2026, took effect on 23 October 2026.
title: Italy AI Laws
subtitle: Law No. 132 of 2025, a national AI law alongside the EU AI Act
body_html:
Status at a glance

Binding national AI law, alongside the EU AI Act. Italy was the first EU member state to pass a national AI law: Law No. 132 of 23 September 2025 (Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale), published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 25 September 2025 and in force since 10 October 2025. It does not duplicate the EU AI Act, which applies in Italy directly; by its own terms it "non produce nuovi obblighi" beyond the Act (art. 3(5)). It names the national authorities, sets rules for minors, copyright and specific sectors, adds criminal offences, and delegates further rules to the government. The first decree under that delegation, Legislative Decree No. 179 of 7 October 2026, took effect on 23 October 2026. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Gazzetta Ufficiale and Normattiva.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
Law on artificial intelligenceLegge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132Gazzetta Ufficiale, Serie Generale n. 223, 25 September 202510 October 2025; government delegations within twelve months (art. 24)
Legislative Decree aligning national law with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the powers of the national authorities, and trainingDecreto legislativo 7 ottobre 2026, n. 179Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 234, 8 October 202623 October 2026
EU AI ActRegulation (EU) 2024/1689Official Journal, 12 July 2024Directly applicable; see the EU AI Act

Who regulates and enforces

  • Agenzia per l'Italia Digitale (AgID): innovation, and the notification, accreditation and monitoring of conformity assessment bodies; the notifying authority (art. 20(1)(a) and (2)).
  • Agenzia per la Cybersicurezza Nazionale (ACN): supervision, including inspections and sanctions; the market surveillance authority and single point of contact under the AI Act (art. 20(1)(b) and (2)).
  • Banca d'Italia, CONSOB and IVASS: market surveillance for the financial sector, as AI Act Article 74(6) provides.
  • The Garante per la protezione dei dati personali and AGCOM keep their powers (art. 20(4)).

Scope and reach

The law covers the research, testing, development, adoption and use of AI systems and models (art. 1), with definitions taken from the EU AI Act (art. 2). Its reach follows the AI Act's: an operator outside Italy that the Act reaches is supervised in Italy by the authorities above.

Core obligations

  • Children under 14 need parental consent to use AI and for the related processing of their data; those aged 14 to 17 may consent themselves (art. 4(4)).
  • Copyright protects only works of human authorship, including works made with AI assistance; text and data mining is limited to what the copyright law already allows (art. 25).
  • Every obligation of the EU AI Act, supervised by AgID and ACN.

What is coming next

  • The remaining decrees under the delegation of art. 24, including on civil and criminal liability for unlawful AI use (art. 24(3)). The twelve-month deadline ran to 10 October 2026, extendable by sixty days (art. 24(4)); whether it was exercised was not confirmed.
